newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt targets seven mln T wheat harvest in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Egypt targets seven mln T wheat harvest in 1997.

text.p: Egypt aims to grow seven million tonnes of wheat next year, the government newspaper al-Ahram said on Thursday, quoting Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali.
In the previous season, which ended in the early summer of this year, the country grew 5.7 million tonnes of wheat, slightly less than it initially hoped.

Wali said 2.5 million acres would be planted with wheat. Last season the area planted was about 2.35 million acres but the yield was very low on 150,000 acres of rainfed land on the northwestern coast, officials said.
Despite dramatic increases in wheat production in the 1990s, Egypt remains a big wheat importer, buying more than four million tonnes a year, mainly from the United States and Europe.
If Egypt meets the 1997 harvest target, the crop would be the biggest ever.

Wali said that in the coming season Egypt would plant higher yielding varieties and would plant new areas in southern Egypt, the Sinai peninsula and the northwestern coast. --Cairo newsroom +20 2 578 3290/1
